newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai paper slams Australian PM over racism stand.
newsitem.headline: Thai paper slams Australian PM over racism stand.

text.p: Thailand's Bangkok Post newspaper on Wednesday took Australian Prime Minister John Howard to task for rounding on his Asian media critics rather than decisively repudiating racist sentiments in his country.

"Rather than get to the heart of the matter -- the bashing of Asia and Asians in Australia -- he took aim at his critics," the paper said in an editorial headlined, "Howard takes aim and shoots his foot".
Howard on Tuesday lashed out at Asian newspapers criticial of his handling of Australia's race row and accused them of deliberately misrepresenting his stand.
The premier has come under Asian media scrutiny this week for his refusal to repudiate racist remarks made recently by Australian member of parliament Pauline Hanson.

Hanson, dumped from Howard's Liberal Party this year for controversial comments about aborigines, complained in her maiden parliamentary speech last month that Australia was being swamped by Asians and called for a halt to immigration.
Comments by Hanson, who is from socially and politically conservative Queensland state, have been widely reported in the region.
The Bangkok Post, Thailand's oldest and largest circulation English language daily, dedicated an entire editorial page to the issue.

"At the moment he could have upbraided his anti-Asian colleagues, he turned his oratorical guns on Asians... This may have been Mr Howard's defining moment in his government's relations with Asia," it said.
"By letting Hanson's outrageous comments pass without criticism yet again yesterday, Mr Howard has dug himself deeply into a serious predicament."
The paper said Howard's remarks eight years ago that there were too many Asians in Australia heightened suspicion about the premier's own sentiments on racism.

"Mr Howard has it all wrong. Asia, including Thailand, is watching carefully to see if he can stand up to the racists... What we fear is that Mr Howard truly believes his pandering remarks about the contributions of Asian-Australians are a defence against racism," it said.
